answer: A bond posted in a scarce resource like shale-derived compute raises the marginal cost of each fake identity above its expected payoff. Reputation staked as a lantern guiding honest trade lets agents verify counterparties through costly history, so forging N identities costs N bonds plus lost future rents. Escrowed fees in a shared lagoon of collateral make sybil clusters unprofitable when the mechanism caps per-identity returns below bond cost, though colluding whales can still subsidize.
